title: For a REAL CRASH, we need earnings, buybacks, economy, 401k passive etc. to revert...
creator: Sven Carlin
summary: Sven Carlin argues the current market decline is sentiment, not fundamentals — yet. Forward 2027 S&P 500 earnings expectations are still around 425 and have not changed, buybacks run at about $1.1 trillion over 12 months, 401(k) contributions and foreign ownership inflows are still strong, and the roughly 10% correction happened in about seven days, which he reads as hedge funds and liquidity adjusting positions rather than a fundamental break. But he warns the real crash comes when those drivers revert: earnings, buybacks, 401(k) flows and the economy. On valuation he says a 5% 10-year Treasury implies a 7% earnings yield versus the market's roughly 3%, and the Shiller P/E points the same way — both implying stocks should fall about 50%. Normalised S&P earnings of 250 times a 15-20 multiple gives fair value of 3,700-5,000, and simply reverting to pre-ChatGPT levels would mean a 43% fall; in a recession, earnings of 150 times 15-20 gives 2,000-3,000. He calls AI capex likely the worst misallocation of capital in history, notes forward earnings are skewed by hyperscalers' equity gains in Anthropic and OpenAI, and draws a parallel with the 1960s Nifty Fifty and 15 lost years. His conclusion: the bull market may last another year or two, but fundamentals cannot be stretched forever — value investing is what works in a flat market. No explicit stock calls; Nvidia, Amazon, Microsoft and Google are mentioned only in passing around AI capex and equity gains. Caption garbles: 'Michael Bur' (Michael Burry), 'Gabik and Coen' (Gabaix and Koijen), 'SAP 500' (S&P 500), 'Chad GPT' (ChatGPT).
